source_defect_corrections.EntityStateShellType_missing_pwsh: Native State shell vocabulary includes pwsh because the source Object supports pwsh and collected shell identity must remain testable.
source_defect_corrections.command_state_datatype: OVAL 5.12.3 shellcommand_state declares command as AnySimple while shellcommand_item collects a string and source documentation requires the command to be echoed verbatim. Native NG uses the collected string datatype so State and Item remain aligned.
source_defect_corrections.stdout_line_state_datatype: OVAL 5.12.3 shellcommand State stdout_line uses AnySimple comparison datatypes, while its collected Item stdout_line is always string. The State comparison datatype governs an explicit OVAL cast at evaluation; Item evidence preserves string. The 0.3 native capability keeps these separate.

command.description: Single command or one-line shell command supplied by the Assessment.

error_if_exit_status_not_0.description: Treat non-zero command exit status as collection error; OVAL default false is materialized.

error_if_stderr_exists.description: Treat any stderr output as collection error; OVAL default false is materialized.

pattern.description: Optional regular expression used to retain matching stdout lines.

shell.description: Shell/interpreter used to execute the command.

semantic_validator_rules.rule: Every Set filter State reference must resolve to capability independent.shellcommand.
When object.pattern is present it is a regular expression applied to stdout lines; matching output lines and capture subexpressions remain separately observable.

Execution of publisher-supplied commands is trust-sensitive. Package/signature verification policy SHALL be enforced outside the command string itself and scanners SHOULD avoid executing unsigned or untrusted content according to deployment policy.

This capability represents command-oriented assessment. It SHALL NOT replace native scanner capabilities when doing so would discard meaningful native collection semantics such as controlled filesystem traversal, structured evidence, or bounded collection.
